```{=html}
<section class="article-section">
  <div class="container">
    <div class="articles-list">
      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>OpenSim Models</h2>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 2rem;">
          <img src="https://opensim.stanford.edu/images/opensim-logo.png" alt="OpenSim Logo" class="software-logo" style="max-width: 250px; margin-bottom: 1rem;" onerror="this.style.display='none'">
          <p style="font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
            OpenSim is a freely available, open-source software platform for modeling, simulating, and analyzing 
            the neuromusculoskeletal system. Developed at Stanford University, OpenSim enables researchers to 
            build and analyze musculoskeletal models, perform inverse kinematics and dynamics, and simulate 
            movement. OpenSim models are particularly valuable for biomechanics research, rehabilitation, and 
            sports science applications, including detailed analysis of golf swing mechanics.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Available Models</h2>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Golf Swing Musculoskeletal Models</h3>
          <p>Full-body musculoskeletal models of the golf swing, including detailed muscle-tendon units, 
          joint kinematics, and force analysis. These models enable analysis of muscle activation patterns, 
          joint torques, and energy transfer throughout the swing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Inverse Kinematics and Dynamics Models</h3>
          <p>Models for performing inverse kinematics (computing joint angles from marker positions) and 
          inverse dynamics (computing joint torques from motion data) for golf swing analysis and other 
          biomechanical movements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Forward Dynamics Simulations</h3>
          <p>Forward dynamics models that simulate movement from muscle activations and external forces, 
          allowing for predictive analysis and optimization of golf swing mechanics.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3>Muscle-Tendon Models</h3>
          <p>Detailed models of muscle-tendon units with Hill-type muscle models, enabling analysis of 
          muscle force production, energy consumption, and coordination patterns in complex movements.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Resources</h2>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="https://simtk.org/projects/opensim" target="_blank" rel="noopener">OpenSim on SimTK</a></h3>
          <p>Access the OpenSim project on SimTK for downloads, documentation, forums, and model repository.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="https://simtk-confluence.stanford.edu:8443/display/OpenSim" target="_blank" rel="noopener">OpenSim Documentation</a></h3>
          <p>Comprehensive documentation including user guides, API reference, tutorials, and examples.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="https://simtk.org/projects/opensim#tabs-3" target="_blank" rel="noopener">OpenSim Model Repository</a></h3>
          <p>Browse and download pre-built musculoskeletal models from the OpenSim model repository.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-list-item">
          <h3><a href="https://simtk.org/forums/viewforum.php?f=91" target="_blank" rel="noopener">OpenSim Forums</a></h3>
          <p>Community forums for asking questions, sharing models, and getting support from the OpenSim community.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="coming-soon">
        <p style="margin-top: 3rem; font-style: italic; color: var(--text-light);">
          OpenSim models and detailed documentation will be added as they are developed. Check back soon!
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
```
